claim: Idiopathic scoliosis (IS) affects about 2.5% of the global population.
source: Idiopathic scoliosis (IS) is the most common form of spinal deformity, affecting about 2.5% of the global population (Hresko, 2013; Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Hresko, 2013; Luk et al., 2010).

claim: IS may have long-term physical and mental health consequences, such as cosmetic deformity, cardiopulmonary impairment, and even disability.
source: IS may have long-term physical and mental health consequences, such as cosmetic deformity, cardiopulmonary impairment, and even disability (Weinstein et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Weinstein et al., 2003.

claim: Early intervention with conservative treatments, such as braces, can control scoliosis progression and reduce the need for surgical intervention.
source: Early intervention with conservative treatments, such as braces, can control scoliosis progression and reduce the need for surgical intervention (Weinstein et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Weinstein et al., 2013.

claim: IS often remains undiagnosed until malformation is evident.
source: However, IS often remains undiagnosed until malformation is evident, emphasizing the importance of risk-prediction measurements in medical management.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact in the manuscript text.

claim: Genetic factors are thought to play a significant role in the development of IS.
source: Genetic factors are thought to play a significant role in the development of IS, while only a few genes have been associated with the condition to date (Cheng et al., 2015; Miller, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cheng et al., 2015 and Miller, 2007.

claim: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with susceptibility to IS have been identified through genome-wide association studies (GWASs), including SNPs linked to genes such as LBX1, GPR126, and BNC2.
source: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with susceptibility to IS have been identified through genome-wide association studies (GWASs), including SNPs linked to genes such as LBX1, GPR126, and BNC2.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact in the manuscript text.

claim: Knockdown or overexpression of zebrafish homologs of IS-associated genes has yielded body axis defects.
source: Notably, knockdown or overexpression of zebrafish homologs of these IS-associated genes has yielded body axis defects (Guo et al., 2016; Kou et al., 2019; Kou et al., 2013; Ogura et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Rare variants in FBN1, FBN2, and other extracellular matrix genes are associated with severe IS.
source: Rare variants in FBN1, FBN2, and other extracellular matrix genes are associated with severe IS (Buchan et al., 2014; Haller et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Buchan et al., 2014 and Haller et al., 2016.

claim: Linkage analysis of familial IS suggests that it follows autosomal dominant (AD), X-linked dominant, and multifactorial patterns of inheritance.
source: Linkage analysis of familial IS suggests that it follows autosomal dominant (AD), X-linked dominant, and multifactorial patterns of inheritance (Miller et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Miller et al., 2005.

claim: Variants in CHD7 and AKAP2 are implicated in the pathogenesis of Mendelian forms of IS.
source: Variants in CHD7 and AKAP2 are also implicated in the pathogenesis of Mendelian forms of IS (Gao et al., 2007; Liebeskind et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2007 and Liebeskind et al., 2016.

claim: Centriolar protein POC5 and planar cell polarity protein Vang-like protein 1 (VANGL1) were shown to be associated with IS.
source: Finally, centriolar protein POC5 and planar cell polarity protein Vang-like protein 1 (VANGL1) were also shown to be associated with IS.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact in the manuscript text.

claim: The mechanisms underlying IS progression still require further investigation.
source: Notably, all these genes participate in a wide range of biological processes, and the mechanisms underlying IS progression still require further investigation.
evidence: The claim is stated as a fact in the manuscript text.

claim: There is currently no consensus on the etiology of IS.
source: Consequently, there is currently no consensus on the etiology of IS (Tang et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tang et al., 2021.

claim: The study developed a novel pipeline that combines SNP-to-gene mapping and rare variant association analysis.
source: In this study, we developed a novel pipeline that combines SNP-to-gene mapping and rare variant association analysis.
evidence: The claim describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The study analyzed a large Chinese population with IS and validated findings in East Asian and European populations.
source: Using this approach, we analyzed a large Chinese population with IS and further validated our findings in East Asian and European populations.
evidence: The claim describes the study design and populations analyzed.

claim: The study identified EPHA4 as a novel gene associated with IS.
source: Through these analyses, we identified EPHA4 as a novel gene associated with IS.
evidence: The claim is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Impaired EPHA4 pathway components and resulting defects in central pattern generators (CPGs) were associated with asymmetric spinal locomotion in zebrafish.
source: To confirm the pathogenicity of this gene, we used a zebrafish model and found that impaired EPHA4 pathway components and resulting defects in central pattern generators (CPGs) were associated with asymmetric spinal locomotion, which may serve as a contributory factor in the development of IS.
evidence: The claim is a primary finding from the zebrafish model experiments.

claim: Mutations in NGEF were identified among IS patients.
source: Additionally, we searched for candidate genes related to EPHA4 signaling pathways and identified mutations in the NGEF among IS patients.
evidence: The claim is a finding from the genetic analysis of IS patients.

claim: The impairment of the EPHA4 pathway and CPGs plays a previously unknown role in the development and progression of IS.
source: Overall, our data suggest that the impairment of the EPHA4 pathway and CPGs plays a previously unknown role in the development and progression of IS.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: 41 SNPs showed genome-wide significance (p<5 × 10−8) in the literature review of IS-associated SNPs.
source: This led us to obtain 41 SNPs that showed genome-wide significance (p<5 × 10−8) as detailed in Supplementary file 1.
evidence: The claim is based on data extraction from published literature.

claim: 156 candidate genes were identified that could be potentially linked to the 41 significant SNPs.
source: We then employed positional mapping, expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) mapping, or chromatin interaction mapping to identify 156 candidate genes that could be potentially linked to these SNPs.
evidence: The claim describes the results of the gene mapping analysis.

claim: EPHA4 was the only significant gene (p=0.045, OR = 4.09) identified from rare variant analysis of 156 candidate genes using exome data from 411 Chinese probands and 3800 unrelated Chinese controls.
source: Further analysis of rare variants for the 156 candidate genes using exome data from 411 Chinese probands and 3800 unrelated Chinese controls identified EPHA4 as the only significant gene (p=0.045, OR = 4.09) (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of genetic data.

claim: EPHA4 is a member of the Eph family of receptor tyrosine kinases which play a vital role in the development of the nervous system.
source: EPHA4 is a member of the Eph family of receptor tyrosine kinases which play a vital role in the development of the nervous system (Kania and Klein, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kania and Klein, 2016.

claim: Three rare variants in EPHA4 were identified from three IS patients, including one splicing-donor variant and two missense variants.
source: We identified three rare variants in EPHA4 from three IS patients, including one splicing-donor variant and two missense variants (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is based on genetic sequencing data from IS patients.

claim: Two of the three rare variants in EPHA4 (NM_004438.3: c.1443+1G>C and c.2546G>A [p.Cys849Tyr]) arose de novo.
source: Of the three rare variants in EPHA4, two (NM_004438.3: c.1443+1G>C and c.2546G>A [p.Cys849Tyr]) arose de novo (Figure 1A and Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on trio sequencing data or Sanger sequencing of parents.

claim: The heterozygous splicing variant (c.1443+1G>C) was identified in a 15-year-old female IS patient (SCO2003P0846).
source: The heterozygous splicing variant (c.1443+1G>C) was identified in a 15-year-old female IS patient (SCO2003P0846) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on genetic sequencing data from a specific patient.

claim: Scoliosis in patient SCO2003P0846 was diagnosed at 13 years of age, with a main curve Cobb angle of 60°.
source: Scoliosis in this patient was diagnosed at 13 years of age, with a main curve Cobb angle of 60°.
evidence: The claim is based on clinical data from the patient.

claim: The c.1443+1G>C variant introduced a new splicing site, resulting in a 36 bp in-frame deletion in exon 6.
source: The in vitro minigene assay showed that the c.1443+1G>C variant introduced a new splicing site, resulting in a 36 bp in-frame deletion in exon 6 (Figure 1G and I, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from a minigene assay.

claim: The EPHA4 heterozygous missense variant (c.2546G>A, p.Cys849Tyr) was identified in a 13-year-old female IS patient (SCO2003P2146).
source: The EPHA4 heterozygous missense variant (c.2546G>A, p.Cys849Tyr), identified in a 13-year-old female IS patient (SCO2003P2146) (Figure 1C), is located in the protein tyrosine kinase domain of EPHA4 protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on genetic sequencing data from a specific patient.

claim: The onset of scoliosis in patient SCO2003P2146 was at 11 years of age with a 70° main curve Cobb angle.
source: The onset of scoliosis in this patient was at 11 years of age with a 70° main curve Cobb angle.
evidence: The claim is based on clinical data from the patient.

claim: EPHA4 plays a critical role in phosphorylating CDK5, which in turn activates downstream signaling pathways.
source: Given the critical role of EPHA4 in phosphorylating CDK5, which in turn activates downstream signaling pathways (Fu et al., 2007), a western blot analysis of the EPHA4-c.2546G>A variant was conducted to investigate the protein expression levels of EPHA4 and CDK5 and the amount of phosphorylated CDK5 (pCDK5) in HEK293T cells transfected with EPHA4-mutant or EPHA4-WT plasmid.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2007.

claim: The missense variant c.2546G>A resulted in a decreased phosphorylation level of CDK5 (p=0.015), suggesting a partial loss-of-function (LoF) of EPHA4.
source: Our results revealed that the missense variant resulted in a decreased phosphorylation level of CDK5 (p=0.015), suggesting a partial loss-of-function (LoF) of EPHA4 (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is based on western blot analysis data.

claim: A de novo heterozygous EPHA4 intronic variant (c.1318+10344A>G) was identified in a 16-year-old female patient (SCO2003P2080).
source: A de novo heterozygous EPHA4 intronic variant (c.1318+10344A>G) was identified in a 16-year-old female patient (SCO2003P2080) (Figure 1D and Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on whole-genome sequencing data from a specific patient.

claim: Patient SCO2003P2080 developed scoliosis at 11 years of age with a 70° main curve Cobb angle.
source: She developed scoliosis at 11 years of age with a 70° main curve Cobb angle.
evidence: The claim is based on clinical data from the patient.

claim: The c.1318+10344A>G variant is predicted to affect the branch point of the fifth intron of EPHA4.
source: This variant is predicted to affect the branch point of the fifth intron of EPHA4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction.

claim: The c.1318+10344A>G variant induced exon 5 skipping, resulting in a 339 bp in-frame deletion.
source: We performed nested PCR to show that this variant induced exon 5 skipping, resulting in a 339 bp in-frame deletion (Figure 1H and J).
evidence: The claim is based on nested PCR experimental data.

claim: A 6-year-old patient (SCO2003P3202) was previously diagnosed with Waardenburg syndrome caused by a 4.46 Mb de novo deletion at 2q35-q36.2.
source: Next, we employed an in-house gene matching approach under the framework of the DISCO study, which identified a 6-year-old patient (SCO2003P3202) who had been previously diagnosed with Waardenburg syndrome caused by a 4.46 Mb de novo deletion at 2q35-q36.2 (Li et al., 2015; Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on genetic data and a citation to Li et al., 2015.

claim: Patient SCO2003P3202 also presented mild scoliosis.
source: Intriguingly, the patient also presented mild scoliosis (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is based on clinical observation of the patient.

claim: The deletion in patient SCO2003P3202 included the entire PAX3 gene and 36 neighboring genes, including EPHA4.
source: The deletion included the entire PAX3 gene, which was responsible for the Waardenburg syndrome phenotype, and 36 neighboring genes, including EPHA4 (Figure 1K).
evidence: The claim is based on genetic analysis of the deletion.

claim: Scoliosis is not typically associated with Waardenburg syndrome caused solely by PAX3 pathogenic variants.
source: As scoliosis is not typically associated with Waardenburg syndrome caused solely by PAX3 pathogenic variants (Tassabehji et al., 1993), we hypothesize that the deletion of EPHA4 may be responsible for the IS phenotype in this patient.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tassabehji et al., 1993.

claim: The deletion of EPHA4 may be responsible for the IS phenotype in patient SCO2003P3202.
source: As scoliosis is not typically associated with Waardenburg syndrome caused solely by PAX3 pathogenic variants (Tassabehji et al., 1993), we hypothesize that the deletion of EPHA4 may be responsible for the IS phenotype in this patient.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on genetic and clinical data.

claim: The GWAS signal rs13398147 represents a significant eQTL in esophagus and colon tissues, with the T allele associated with decreased expression of EPHA4.
source: Notably, the GWAS signal which we mapped to EPHA4 (rs13398147) (Zhu et al., 2015) represents a significant eQTL in esophagus and colon tissues, with the T allele associated with decreased expression of EPHA4.
evidence: The claim is based on GWAS and eQTL data, with a citation to Zhu et al., 2015.

claim: Two eQTLs in EPHA4 associated with decreased expression of EPHA4 in brain tissue were identified in the East Asian GWAS cohort.
source: In our East Asian GWAS cohort of 6449 adolescent IS patients and 158,068 controls, we identified another two eQTLs in EPHA4 associated with decreased expression of EPHA4 in brain tissue (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is based on GWAS and eQTL analysis data.

claim: Common SNPs in EPHA4, after aggregation, showed significant enrichment (p=0.023) in IS patients vs controls in the East Asian GWAS cohort.
source: In the same GWAS cohort, common SNPs in EPHA4, after aggregation, also showed significant enrichment (p=0.023) in IS patients vs controls.
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of GWAS data.

claim: The convergence between rare and common variants of EPHA4 that lead to LoF or hypomorphic effects highlights the pivotal role of EPHA4 in the pathogenesis of IS.
source: Taken together, the convergence between rare and common variants of EPHA4 that lead to LoF or hypomorphic effects highlights the pivotal role of EPHA4 in the pathogenesis of IS.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined genetic data.

claim: Zebrafish have two homologs of EPHA4, epha4a and epha4b.
source: Zebrafish have two homologs of EPHA4, epha4a and epha4b.
evidence: The claim is based on known zebrafish genetics.

claim: A stable epha4a zebrafish mutant line with a 63 bp deletion in exon 3 was established using CRISPR-Cas9.
source: Using CRISPR-Cas9, we established a stable epha4a zebrafish mutant line with a 63 bp deletion in exon 3, which introduced a stop codon and resulted in a truncated protein (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from zebrafish genetic manipulation.

claim: The homozygous epha4a mutant larvae had no apparent defects in either notochord or body axis development.
source: The homozygous epha4a mutant larvae had no apparent defects in either notochord or body axis development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on observation of zebrafish larvae.

claim: The hindbrain rhombomeric boundaries were found to be defective in both the epha4a homozygous mutants and morphants.
source: Consistent with previous reports, the hindbrain rhombomeric boundaries were found to be defective in both the epha4a homozygous mutants and morphants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Cayuso et al., 2019; Cooke et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and supported by citations to Cayuso et al., 2019 and Cooke et al., 2005.

claim: More than 75% adult epha4a mutants showed mild scoliosis (88 of 116), and some mutants exhibited severe scoliotic phenotype (4 of 116).
source: Interestingly, more than 75% adult mutants showed mild scoliosis (88 of 116), and some mutants exhibited severe scoliotic phenotype (4 of 116) (Figure 2C and D, Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative observation of adult zebrafish mutants.

claim: Some heterozygous adult epha4a mutants also developed mild scoliosis (14 of 95), whereas none of the wild-type fish showed any signs of scoliosis (0 of 76).
source: Remarkably, some heterozygous adult mutants also developed mild scoliosis (14 of 95), whereas none of the wild-type fish showed any signs of scoliosis (0 of 76) (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative observation of adult zebrafish.

claim: The epha4b zebrafish mutants with a 25 bp deletion in exon 3 also developed mild scoliosis (28 of 43).
source: Similarly, we further generated the epha4b mutants with a 25 bp deletion in exon 3, which resulted in a frameshift mutation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A). The epha4b zebrafish mutants also developed mild scoliosis (28 of 43) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from zebrafish genetic manipulation and observation.

claim: Both epha4a and epha4b mutants exhibited early onset scoliosis starting from around 20 days post-fertilization.
source: Intriguingly, both epha4a and epha4b mutants exhibited early onset scoliosis starting from around 20 days post-fertilization (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D), a stage similar to that of IS patients.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of zebrafish mutants over time.

claim: Mutations in Epha4 proteins are linked to the scoliotic phenotype in zebrafish.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that mutations in Epha4 proteins are linked to the scoliotic phenotype in zebrafish.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the zebrafish experimental data.

claim: The motion distance and swimming velocity were significantly decreased in epha4a mutants at 8 days post-fertilization.
source: By monitoring the swimming behavior of 8 days post-fertilization (dpf) zebrafish larvae, we found the motion distance and swimming velocity were significantly decreased in epha4a mutants (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on behavioral analysis data from zebrafish larvae.

claim: The wild-type group changed their swimming direction randomly, showing a relative angle around 0°.
source: The wild-type group changed their swimming direction randomly, showing a relative angle around 0° (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is based on behavioral analysis data from wild-type zebrafish larvae.

claim: The epha4a mutants favored turning to one side of their directions (a positive angle reflects a leftward turn).
source: In contrast, the epha4a mutants favored turning to one side of their directions (a positive angle reflects a leftward turn) (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is based on behavioral analysis data from epha4a mutant zebrafish larvae.

claim: The absolute turn angles and turning speed (angular velocity) were significantly higher in epha4a mutants.
source: Moreover, the absolute turn angles and turning speed (angular velocity) were significantly higher in these mutants (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: The claim is based on behavioral analysis data from epha4a mutant zebrafish larvae.

claim: Injection of epha4a mRNA into epha4a mutants significantly restored the swimming coordination defects.
source: To rule out potential off-target effects, we injected epha4a mRNA into epha4a mutants, which significantly restored the swimming coordination defects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on rescue experiment data.

claim: In sibling controls, the larvae responded to the tactile stimulation and swam away quickly.
source: In sibling controls, the larvae responded to the tactile stimulation and swam away quickly (Video 3).
evidence: The claim is based on behavioral observation of control zebrafish larvae.

claim: The epha4a mutants failed to respond to the initial stimulation, and the swimming pattern was defective with an abnormal bending pattern (37 of 62 from tail-stimulation group and 34 of 77 from head-stimulation group).
source: Conversely, the epha4a mutants failed to respond to the initial stimulation, and the swimming pattern was defective with an abnormal bending pattern (37 of 62 from tail-stimulation group and 34 of 77 from head-stimulation group) (Figure 3G, Video 4).
evidence: The claim is based on behavioral observation of epha4a mutant zebrafish larvae.

claim: After tactile stimulation, wild-type larvae displayed a high-speed C-bend turn followed by a weaker counterbend turn after several milliseconds.
source: After tactile stimulation, wild-type larvae displayed a high-speed C-bend turn followed by a weaker counterbend turn after several milliseconds (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: The claim is based on high-speed video analysis of wild-type zebrafish larvae.

claim: The turning angles of the control larvae after stimulation changed with a sinusoidal wave pattern.
source: The turning angles of the control larvae after stimulation changed with a sinusoidal wave pattern (Figure 3J).
evidence: The claim is based on high-speed video analysis of control zebrafish larvae.

claim: The turning pattern in epha4a mutants was dramatically different from wild-type larvae.
source: In contrast, this pattern was dramatically different in epha4a mutants (Figure 3I and K).
evidence: The claim is based on high-speed video analysis of epha4a mutant zebrafish larvae.

claim: Although the C-bend turning angles were similar between epha4a mutants and control siblings, the turning angles of the counterbend decreased significantly.
source: Of note, although the C-bend turning angles were similar between epha4a mutants and control siblings, the turning angles of the counterbend decreased significantly (Figure 3L), implying a left/right coordination defect.
evidence: The claim is based on high-speed video analysis comparing epha4a mutants and controls.

claim: Both regular swimming and tactile stimulation analyses suggested that the left-right coordination swimming pattern is compromised in the absence of Epha4a.
source: Taken together, both regular swimming and tactile stimulation analyses suggested that the left-right coordination swimming pattern is compromised in the absence of Epha4a.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on multiple behavioral analyses.

claim: The coordinated left-right locomotion of zebrafish larvae relies on the synchronized contraction of muscle fibers, a process regulated by motor neurons situated on each side of the fish.
source: The coordinated left-right locomotion of zebrafish larvae relies on the synchronized contraction of muscle fibers, a process regulated by motor neurons situated on each side of the fish.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge of zebrafish locomotion.

claim: In wild-type larvae, the calcium signals exhibited an alternating pattern between the left and right sides of the body.
source: In wild-type larvae, the calcium signals exhibited an alternating pattern between the left and right sides of the body, whereas this coordinated pattern was disrupted in both epha4a mutants and morphants (Figure 4A–B vs A'–B', Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B vs A'–B', Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: The claim is based on calcium imaging data from wild-type zebrafish larvae.

claim: The coordinated calcium signal pattern was disrupted in both epha4a mutants and morphants.
source: In wild-type larvae, the calcium signals exhibited an alternating pattern between the left and right sides of the body, whereas this coordinated pattern was disrupted in both epha4a mutants and morphants (Figure 4A–B vs A'–B', Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B vs A'–B', Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: The claim is based on calcium imaging data from epha4a mutants and morphants.

claim: The activation frequency of motor neurons on the left and right sides was comparable in wild-type larvae, but significantly different in the absence of Epha4a.
source: Additionally, we found that the activation frequency of motor neurons on the left and right sides was comparable in wild-type larvae, but significantly different in the absence of Epha4a (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of calcium imaging data.

claim: In control larvae, the large Mauthner neurons, along with other RS neurons, were symmetrically positioned on each side of the midline and projected their axons to the contralateral sides.
source: In control larvae, the large Mauthner neurons, along with other RS neurons, were symmetrically positioned on each side of the midline and projected their axons to the contralateral sides (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence imaging of control zebrafish larvae.

claim: In epha4a mutant larvae, the mutant axons failed to traverse the midline and instead extended ipsilaterally.
source: However, in epha4a mutant larvae, we observed an abnormal pattern in axonal projections. Specifically, the mutant axons failed to traverse the midline and instead extended ipsilaterally (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence imaging of epha4a mutant zebrafish larvae.

claim: The distance between Mauthner neurons (rhombomere 4) and rhombomere 7 was significantly decreased in epha4a mutant larvae.
source: In addition, the distance between Mauthner neurons (rhombomere 4) and rhombomere 7 was significantly decreased, and rhombomere 5 was scarcely visible in the mutant larvae (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of immunofluorescence imaging.

claim: The sites of axon crossing between two Mauthner neurons tended to deviate to one side of the midline in the epha4a mutants.
source: Furthermore, the sites of axon crossing between two Mauthner neurons tended to deviate to one side of the midline in the mutants (Figure 5C–D').
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of immunofluorescence imaging.

claim: Cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs) represent a unique type of interneuron responsible for modulating the V0 and V2a interneurons, which are integral components of locomotor CPGs.
source: Cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs) represent a unique type of interneuron responsible for modulating the V0 and V2a interneurons, which are integral components of locomotor CPGs (Fidelin et al., 2015; Talpalar et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fidelin et al., 2015, Talpalar et al., 2013, and Wu et al., 2021.

claim: In wild-type larvae, the ascending axons of CSF-cNs projected either to the right or left side from the midline.
source: In wild-type larvae, we observed that the ascending axons of these neurons projected either to the right or left side from the midline, as visualized using Tg(pkd2l1:GAL4;UAS:Kaede) double transgenic larvae (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is based on fluorescence imaging of wild-type zebrafish larvae.

claim: In the absence of Epha4a, the projection of CSF-cNs exhibited notable disorganization, with numerous axons crossing the midline from one side of the trunk.
source: However, in the absence of Epha4a, the projection of these neurons exhibited notable disorganization, with numerous axons crossing the midline from one side of the trunk. This disorganized pattern was observed in both heterozygotic and homozygotic mutants (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on fluorescence imaging of epha4a mutant zebrafish larvae.

claim: In wild-type larvae, tail oscillations following optical stimulation exhibited a symmetrical left-right beating pattern.
source: In wild-type larvae, these tail oscillations exhibited a symmetrical left-right beating pattern (Figure 6C and D, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is based on optogenetic stimulation and video analysis of wild-type zebrafish larvae.

claim: A striking disruption of symmetry was observed in epha4a morphants, as they consistently beat toward one side of the trunk following optical stimulation.
source: However, a striking disruption of this symmetry was observed in epha4a morphants, as they consistently beat toward one side of the trunk following optical stimulation (a positive angle reflects a rightward turn; Figure 6C'–D' and E, Video 10).
evidence: The claim is based on optogenetic stimulation and video analysis of epha4a morphant zebrafish larvae.

claim: The left-right coordination deficiencies observed in epha4a mutants arise from abnormal neural circuit formation, which consequently disrupts the integrity of the CPGs.
source: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the left-right coordination deficiencies observed in epha4a mutants arise from abnormal neural circuit formation, which consequently disrupts the integrity of the CPGs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings.

claim: Both epha4a and epha4b were abundantly expressed in the zebrafish spinal cord.
source: Whole-mount in situ hybridization results showed that both epha4a and epha4b were abundantly expressed in the zebrafish spinal cord (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on in situ hybridization data.

claim: epha4a and epha4b were both expressed in interneurons, suggesting a role for epha4 in interneuron function.
source: We plotted the expression of these two genes using two published single-cell transcriptome data, which showed that epha4a and epha4b were both expressed in interneurons, suggesting a role for epha4 in interneuron function (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B; Cavone et al., 2021; Scott et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on single-cell transcriptome data analysis, with citations to Cavone et al., 2021 and Scott et al., 2021.

claim: The expression of efnb3b, encoding the ligand of Epha4, was highly enriched in the midline floor plate cells.
source: Notably, the expression of efnb3b, encoding the ligand of Epha4, was highly enriched in the midline floor plate cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on single-cell transcriptome data analysis.

claim: Ephrins, through interacting with Eph receptors, play a critical role in repulsive axon guidance during neural development.
source: Ephrins, through interacting with Eph receptors, play a critical role in repulsive axon guidance during neural development (Egea and Klein, 2007; Flanagan and Vanderhaeghen, 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Egea and Klein, 2007 and Flanagan and Vanderhaeghen, 1998.

claim: The efnb3b morphants displayed axon guidance defects, as well as uncoordinated calcium activation.
source: Similar to those of epha4a mutants, the efnb3b morphants also displayed axon guidance defects, as well as uncoordinated calcium activation (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: The claim is based on imaging data from efnb3b morphant zebrafish larvae.

claim: efnb3b morphant larvae displayed left-right oscillation defects after optogenetic stimulation.
source: In addition, morphants larvae also displayed left-right oscillation defects after optogenetic stimulation (a positive angle reflects a rightward turn) (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: The claim is based on optogenetic stimulation and video analysis of efnb3b morphant zebrafish larvae.

claim: A heterozygous de novo start-loss variant (c.1A>G, p.Met1?) in NGEF was identified in a 17-year-old male (SCO2003P3332).
